Prevention: Pruning may help in reducing prolonged wetness which is ideal for disease development
Remove old diseased branches, leaves and twigs from orchard before planting new trees
Monitoring: Check for brownish black sunken spots on leaves, twigs and inflorensence especially under warm, humid conditions
Check for dark affected areas from the tip backwards on new twigs and defoliation of new shoots in severe cases defoliation of the young shoots.
Check for dark sunken lesions on the fruits usually as they mature

Check for linear necrotic regions on the fruit that may or may not be associated with superficial cracking of the epidermis, which may even cause fruits to develop wide, deep cracks in the epidermis that extend into the pulp
Direct Control: Remove all the dead leaves, twigs from the mango farm and burn them
Where possible destroy all flowers that have failed to set fruits
Pluck and destroy all infected fruits
Restrictions: M45) at a dilution rate of 20g/10L of water when flowers appear but before flowers open.
Carry out second spray at fruit set and repeat there after at 14-21 day intervals.
Apply a full cover spray if you have a mist brower (motorized sprayer), although a knapsack sprayer can be used in the nursery.
Do not apply after fruits reach golf ball size.
U - Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use
Hydroxide at a rate of 20g/10L of water at 4 weeks interval from end of flowering up harvest.
During extended wet weather, spray every 14 days.
